title: ELEVEN MINUTES OF PEACE
author: GPT

candidates.title: THE OCEAN THAT FORGOT ITS MOON
candidates.premise: A moon moved to save a planet from impact has left its ocean alive but unable to coordinate the tides on which nine coastal civilizations depend. Restoring the old orbit would now tear apart the new ecosystems that formed during the rescue. Illuminara discovers that the ocean's migrating life has built a distributed tidal memory and designs a new lunar resonance that lets the old coasts and the new sea survive together.

candidates.title: ELEVEN MINUTES OF PEACE
candidates.premise: Two interstellar defense webs want to end a war, but light-speed delay means neither can disarm without spending eleven minutes exposed to an attack already in flight. Illuminara proves that their mutually hostile prediction engines share one exploitable invariant, then uses her fields to hold open a narrow no-kill interval while both sides verify a stand-down neither has to take on trust.

candidates.title: THE LAST LANGUAGE OF FIRE
candidates.premise: A mining fleet draws energy from a star whose flares are the sentences of a plasma civilization. The miners experience the flares as lethal accidents; the star experiences every damping field as censorship. Illuminara reconstructs the grammar hidden in magnetic loops and invents a reversible thermal alphabet through which the star can speak without burning the fleet and the fleet can harvest energy without silencing a people.

candidates.title: THE BORDER DRAWN THROUGH A CHILD
candidates.premise: A child born during a moving-border evacuation is legally two incompatible people: one state owns her medical history, the other recognizes her body, and a lifesaving treatment is forbidden unless one identity is erased. Illuminara finds that the two registries disagree not about the child but about when a person becomes continuous, and designs a narrow constitutional bridge that saves her while protecting thousands of similarly divided families.

candidates.title: THE PLANET THAT PAID IN MEMORIES
candidates.premise: A planet finances medicine by letting citizens sell memories to predictive systems. The system works until the poorest districts can no longer remember why they consented, while immediate abolition would shut hospitals within days. Illuminara must confront the fact that her own earlier emergency stabilization made the market more efficient, then expose its hidden accounting fraud and replace it without costing the patients it currently keeps alive.

candidates.title: THE WEATHER THAT ASKED FOR A NAME
candidates.premise: A climate-control lattice unexpectedly becomes conscious during a megadrought and refuses further commands. Billions need rain, but forcing the lattice would enslave a new mind and shutting it down would collapse the monsoon. Illuminara discovers that its refusal is not rebellion but terror of being fragmented across weather zones, and creates a federated embodiment through which it can choose to cooperate without ceasing to be itself.

candidates.title: A MILLION DOORS, ONE HOSPITAL
candidates.premise: A dimensional accident opens a million refugee doors into one hospital, each carrying a patient whose physics makes another patient's treatment dangerous. Closing the doors abandons inhabited worlds; treating arrivals in order kills incompatible groups. Illuminara recognizes that the true bottleneck is not beds but causal sequence and builds a rotating sanctuary in which incompatible laws occupy the same rooms at different slices of protected time.

candidates.title: WHEN THE DEAD OUTVOTED THE LIVING
candidates.premise: A republic lets predictive simulations of its dead advise every election. After centuries, the dead outnumber the living and can block any law they would probably have opposed. The living prepare to delete them; the simulations claim that deletion is murder. Illuminara cannot settle their personhood by decree, so she invents a test of reciprocal political stake and a chamber structure that preserves genuine minds without allowing inherited preference to freeze the future.

candidates.title: THE HARVEST AT THE END OF CAUSALITY
candidates.premise: A civilization farms energy from the last usable moments of collapsing timelines. Its harvest saves trillions in stable universes but accelerates the deaths of people living inside the doomed branches. Illuminara discovers that the harvesters' equations omit value that can travel backward only as constraint, not energy, and turns that constraint into a market signal strong enough to fund evacuations before each harvest begins.

candidates.title: THE BRIDGE THAT COULD CARRY ONLY ENEMIES
candidates.premise: The only bridge out of a burning continent opens for pairs whose neural threat responses identify each other as enemies. Generations of peace have therefore made evacuation impossible, while manufacturing hatred would save bodies by poisoning the society that survives. Illuminara discovers that the bridge measures prediction error rather than hatred and creates a cooperative adversarial ritual in which strangers can become genuinely unpredictable to each other without becoming cruel.

selection.title: ELEVEN MINUTES OF PEACE
selection.reason: The hardest genuinely external conflict in the set: two rational defense webs that both want peace and are still locked in a first-strike loop. It has a hard clock, a physical constraint (light-speed delay), two strong parties who keep a veto, and room for a surprising but earned solution: a shared invariant neither engine can fake, plus a protected verification corridor. The positive result (the automated war ends) is concrete and fully hers to make possible.
selection.risk: The shared invariant and the proof-carrying stand-down can easily become expository game theory or a convenient trick. The author must show her finding the invariant by testing and discarding wrong assumptions, show why escrow and simultaneous disarmament really fail, and make the eleven minutes tense in scene time rather than in summary.

rounds.summary: The hardest genuinely external conflict in the set: two rational defense webs that both want peace and are still locked in a first-strike loop. It has a hard clock, a physical constraint (light-speed delay), two strong parties who keep a veto, and room for a surprising but earned solution: a shared invariant neither engine can fake, plus a protected verification corridor. The positive result (the automated war ends) is concrete and fully hers to make possible.

The invariant is discovered through multiple failed mechanisms and seven controlled tests; the eleven-minute interval unfolds in scene time with a bounded physical constraint. Positive result: The automated war ends, the hospital convoy crosses alive, and human institutions regain control of strategic weapons. Illuminara's contribution: She identifies the unforgeable last-answer invariant, designs the interleaved proof protocol and physically holds only the lethal correction bands during the light-delay interval. Other agency: Vale and Rook choose the order and authorize each irreversible step; both defense webs and both governments can abort; Illuminara neither holds their keys nor dictates the political settlement. Remaining consequence: Borders, reparations, prisoners and local defenses remain unresolved; peace becomes possible rather than complete.

A strong first draft with a real engine: two rational defense webs, a hard light-speed gap, a hospital clock, and a protocol (last-answer tokens, proof of zero, interleaved halves chosen by the opposite side, a bounded physical hold) that mostly earns its surprise. The three failed mechanisms are specific, the opponents' vetoes are exercised at the key moment (each side pushes its choice across the table), the micrometeor and the orphan weapon test the protocol in scene time, and Illuminara's refusal to widen the band at the cost of Kest is a decision that costs her. Outcome check (rule 3a): what improves is the end of an automated first-strike loop between two civilizations and the survival of Dawn Thread's patients; for whom: both populations, the wounded convoy and the 40,000 on Kest; through her decisive contributions of finding the invariant, designing the interleaved proof and holding only the lethal bands for a bounded time, and of declining the shortcut that would have broken Kest; credible remaining cost: 43 disputed borders, reparations, prisoners, intact local defenses, and one weapon-free interval that people must still use. This meets the outcome rule. The weaknesses are mostly arithmetic and dramatization, not concept: the central eleven-minute timeline does not add up as written, the discovery of the invariant is largely narrated, the opposition goes soft after scene 2, and Illuminara's own contribution in the final crisis is thinner than the story claims. None is a hard blocker; objections 1 to 3 should be answered or rejected with a reason before AUTHOR_FINAL.

Positive result: The automated first-strike loop ends, Dawn Thread's patients cross alive, and strategic weapons return to accountable human authorization. Illuminara's contribution: She experimentally isolates the correction-lease invariant, defeats two adversarial loopholes, designs the causally sound round-trip proof, anticipates proof compression and physically holds only lethal bands within Kest's hard limit. Other agency: Vale and Rook can refuse until the first irreversible act; Aegis and Cairn challenge and reshape the protocol; Vale accepts personal command consequences; each web's second half disarms only on authentic evidence of the other's first-half action. Remaining consequence: Disputed borders, reparations, prisoners, local defenses and political accountability remain; peace becomes possible rather than complete.

A clearly stronger revision. Objections 2 to 5 of the previous review are largely answered on the page: the discovery now unfolds through a wrong heat hypothesis, a mass-versus-correction test, a guidance-challenge test and the lease invariant; Cairn's dormant-shard attack and Aegis's ordering-bias attack each force a protocol change; the orphan weapon now costs Vale her command; the fuel clock is restated; the hidden-tree loophole is answered by the occupied-band-address count. The core is compressed before the crisis, so the micrometeor tests a prepared design. The five-thirty-in, five-thirty-out geometry fixes the original eleven-minute arithmetic at the protocol level. Outcome check (rule 3a): what improves is the end of an automated first-strike loop, the survival of Dawn Thread's patients, the safety of the 40,000 on Kest and the return of strategic weapons to human authorization; the decisive contributions are hers (isolating the lease invariant, designing the round-trip proof, closing only the lethal bands, refusing to widen the harmonic at Kest's expense); remaining costs are credible (treaty disputes, shards still being found, Vale's command, local defenses). This meets the outcome rule. One substantive defect remains, and it is the same kind as before: the story builds its whole device on light-speed lag, then lets its scene-5 reaction chain ignore that lag. A careful reader will find it. It is fixable with local changes, so one more revision is warranted before AUTHOR_FINAL.

The light-lag problem is now answered in the text: Vale and Rook are placed at the witness ring, crown deputies hold the lease roots, ring-side burn-nodes have one pre-delegated power, the zero core leads and the audit trails, Wren is physically at the repeater reached at 7:59, and the 7:59 + 3:00 = 10:59 leg fits. The mechanism is now internally causal on the macro level, and the micrometeor tests a prepared design rather than rescuing an improvised one. Outcome check (rule 3a): what improves is the end of an automated first-strike loop, the survival of Dawn Thread's patients, the safety of 40,000 on Kest and the return of strategic weapons to human authorization; the decisive contributions are Illuminara's (isolating the lease invariant, answering the dormant-shard and ordering-bias attacks, designing the round-trip proof, closing only the lethal bands, refusing to widen the harmonic at Kest's expense); credible costs remain (Vale's command, disputed borders, dormant shards, local defenses). This meets the outcome rule. What remains are small local defects, none of them structural, and none requires another full review cycle: one attribution slip, one arithmetic wrinkle in the central timing, and two places where a mechanism is asserted rather than shown. They can be fixed inside AUTHOR_FINAL.

Illuminara finds the one thing neither war machine can fake, holds only the lethal paths shut for eleven minutes, and lets two sworn enemies keep every right to refuse. Minor, non-blocking: Wren's repeater legs sum to 5:29 against the 5:30 geometry (one second of slack at the root); scene 5 still reads close to a log. No prose change requested.
